question: The Bhakhra Nangal dam is built on which river?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Sutlej**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Bhakhra Nangal dam is built on the Sutlej river, which is one of the major rivers in the northern part of India.
 
• The dam is situated on the border between the states of Himachal Pradesh and Punjab.
 
• The Bhakhra Nangal dam is one of the highest gravity dams in the world, standing at a height of 226 meters.
 
• The primary purpose of the dam is to provide irrigation, flood control, and hydroelectric power generation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sutlej River:**

 
 
• The Sutlej is the longest of the five rivers that flow through the historic crossroads region of Punjab in northern India and Pakistan.
 
• It originates from Lake Rakshastal in Tibet near Mount Kailash and flows through the Indian states of Punjab and Himachal Pradesh before entering Pakistan.
 
• The river is a key tributary of the Indus River system.
 
• The Sutlej River plays a critical role in the agricultural economy of the regions it traverses, providing essential water resources for irrigation.
 
 
 
• **Bhakra Nangal Dam:**
 
 
• The Bhakra Dam is a concrete gravity dam on the Sutlej River in Bilaspur, Himachal Pradesh in northern India.
 
• The dam forms the Gobind Sagar reservoir, which has a capacity of 9.34 billion cubic meters.
 
• The Nangal Dam is located downstream of the Bhakra Dam and serves to divert water for irrigation purposes.
 
• The Bhakra-Nangal project is a joint venture between the Indian states of Punjab, Haryana, and Rajasthan.
 
• The hydroelectric power generated by the dam is distributed among the northern states of India.
 
 
 
• **Gravity Dam:**
 
 
• A gravity dam is a type of dam that relies on its own weight to resist the horizontal pressure of the water pushing against it.
 
• Gravity dams are typically constructed from concrete or stone masonry.
 
• They are designed to hold back large volumes of water and are characterized by their massive size and stability.
 
• Examples of gravity dams include the Hoover Dam in the United States and the Bhakra Dam in India.
 
 
 
• **Hydroelectric Power Generation:**
 
 
• Hydroelectric power is generated by using the energy of falling or flowing water to turn turbines, which then drive generators to produce electricity.
 
• It is a renewable and clean source of energy, as it does not produce greenhouse gas emissions during operation.
 
• Hydroelectric plants can provide a stable and reliable source of electricity, particularly in regions with abundant water resources.
 
• In addition to generating power, hydroelectric dams often provide benefits such as flood control, water supply, and recreational opportunities.
